title: C# Questions & Answers - Introduction of Stream Classes

description: This section of our 1000+ C# MCQs focuses on introduction of stream classes in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: Select the namespace on which the stream classes are defined?
questions.explanation: The core stream classes are defined within the System.IO namespace. To use these classes, you will usually include the following statement near the top of your program: using System.IO;

questions.question: Choose the class on which all stream classes are defined?
questions.explanation: The core stream class is System.IO.Stream. Stream represents a byte stream and is a base class for all other stream classes. It is also abstract, which means that you cannot instantiate a Stream object. Stream defines a set of standard stream operations.

questions.question: Choose the stream class method which is used to close the connection?
The method used to write a single byte to an output stream?
questions.explanation: Writes a single byte to an output stream.

questions.question: Select the method which writes the contents of the stream to the physical device.
questions.explanation:

questions.question: Select the method which returns the number of bytes from the array buffer:

options.text: int Write(byte[] buffer, int offset, int count)

questions.explanation: Writes a subrange of count bytes from the array buffer, beginning at buffer[offset], returning the number of bytes written.

questions.question: Name the method which returns integer as -1 when the end of file is encountered.
questions.explanation: Returns an integer representation of the next available byte of input. Returns -1 when the end of the file is encountered.

questions.question: Select the statements which define the stream.

options.text: A stream is an abstraction that produces or consumes information
A stream is linked to a physical device by the I/0 system

questions.question: Select the action of the method long seek()?

options.text: Attempts to readup to count bytes into buffer starting at buffer[offset]
Writes a single byte to an output stream
Sets the current position in the stream to the specified offset from specified origin and hence returns the new position

questions.explanation:
long Seek(long offset, SeekOrigin origin)

Sets the current position in the stream to the specified offset from the specified origin. It returns the new position.
